items.stem:
Mrs Haddad drives 90 km at an average speed of 60 km/h.
She then drives a further 100 km at an average speed of 80 km/h.

parts.t:
Calculate the total time for the journey.
Give your answer in hours.

Calculate her average speed for the whole journey.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

ms:
M1 for 90 ÷ 60 (= 1.5) or 100 ÷ 80 (= 1.25)
A1
oe, accept 2 h 45 min

M1 for 190 ÷ their 2.75
A1
accept 69.09…; 70 (the mean of the two speeds) scores 0
sols: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 190 ÷ 2.75
Note: the answer is not (60 + 80) ÷ 2 = 70, because more time is spent at the slower speed.

items.stem: A cheetah can run at a top speed of 28 m/s.

parts.t: Change 28 m/s into kilometres per hour.

Calculate the time the cheetah takes to run 1 kilometre at this speed.
Give your answer in seconds, correct to 3 significant figures.

sols: In one second the cheetah travels 28 m, so in one hour it travels 28 × 3600 = 100 800 m.
1 kilometre = 1000 metres, so work in metres and seconds.

items.stem:
A lorry leaves a depot at 08 00 and travels along a straight road at a constant speed of 60 km/h.
A car leaves the same depot at 09 00 and travels along the same road at a constant speed of 90 km/h.

parts.t: Work out how far the lorry has travelled by 09 00.
Find the time at which the car catches up with the lorry.
Work out how far from the depot the car catches up with the lorry.

ms:
M1 for 90 − 60 = 30 (the speed the car gains) oe, or for 60t + 60 = 90t
M1 for their 60 ÷ their 30 = 2 hours
A1
cao
sols: The lorry travels for 1 hour before the car starts.
At 09 00 the car is 60 km behind the lorry.
Each hour the car gains 90 − 60 = 30 km.
this is the relative speed of the car compared with the lorry
Time to close the gap = 60 ÷ 30 = 2 hours.
The car catches up at 09 00 + 2 hours = 11 00
Check: at 11 00 the lorry has travelled 60 × 3 = 180 km and the car 90 × 2 = 180 km ✓
The car has been travelling for 2 hours at 90 km/h.

items.stem:
A delivery van travels 100 km at an average speed of x km/h.
On the return journey its average speed is (x + 10) km/h and the journey takes 30 minutes less.

parts.t: Show that x2 + 10x − 2000 = 0.
Solve x2 + 10x − 2000 = 0 to find the average speed on the first journey.

Work out the time taken for the first journey.
Give your answer in hours.

ms:
M1 for both times written as 100⁄x and 100⁄x + 10
M1 for a difference of 1⁄2 (not 30) and multiplying by 2x(x + 10)
A1 for correct completion, nfww

M1 for (x + 50)(x − 40) oe or correct use of the formula
A1
−50 must be rejected, cao
sols: Time for the first journey = 100⁄x hours.
Time for the return journey = 100⁄x + 10 hours.
the return journey is the quicker one, so it is subtracted
Factorise: two numbers with product −2000 and sum +10 are +50 and −40.
A speed cannot be negative, so x = 40 km/h
Check: the return journey takes 100 ÷ 50 = 2 hours, which is 30 minutes less ✓
